issues.title: MCP model silently drops harness-specific keys (e.g. Claude Code `oauth`) — no passthrough for remote-MCP OAuth client config
issues.body:
## Summary

apm's MCP dependency model carries only a fixed field set and silently discards any other keys on render. There is no way to express harness-specific MCP config that apm doesn't model, notably Claude Code's remote-MCP `oauth` block (`clientId` / `callbackPort`). For a remote MCP server that requires a pre-registered OAuth client because it does not support Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591), this makes the server unusable when configured through apm.

## Environment

- Reproduced on apm 0.15.0; confirmed still present in source on v0.17.0 (latest).
- Target: Claude Code (`.mcp.json`).

## What happens

`MCPDependency` (`src/apm_cli/models/dependency/mcp.py`) models only:
`name, transport, env, args, version, registry, package, headers, tools, url, command`.

- `from_dict`: "Unknown keys are silently ignored for forward compatibility."
- `to_dict`: serializes only that whitelist.

So this `apm.yml`:

```yaml
dependencies:
  mcp:
    - name: slack
      registry: false
      transport: http
      url: https://mcp.slack.com/mcp
      oauth:
        clientId: "<pre-registered-client-id>"
        callbackPort: 3118
```

produces a generated `.mcp.json` slack entry with no `oauth` key. No warning is emitted; `apm install` reports success.

## Why it matters (concrete failure)

Claude Code's `.mcp.json` supports an `oauth` block to pin a pre-registered OAuth client. Slack's remote MCP (`https://mcp.slack.com/mcp`) does not support Dynamic Client Registration, so without a pre-registered `clientId` Claude Code's OAuth fails with:

> SDK auth failed: Incompatible auth server: does not support dynamic client registration

Because apm cannot carry the `oauth` block, a Slack MCP configured via apm cannot authenticate. The same applies to any remote MCP needing harness-specific auth config apm doesn't model.

## Two distinct problems

1. **No passthrough for harness-specific MCP fields.** The universal model is a lowest-common-denominator with no escape hatch (e.g. a per-harness `claude:` / `extra:` map) to round-trip fields verbatim into the target manifest.
2. **Silent drop.** Unknown keys are discarded with no warning, so a user who supplies the correct field name gets no signal it was ignored. It fails closed and silently.

Note: `apm pack` already strips credential-shaped keys from the Claude `.mcp.json` manifest, which suggests apm knows `.mcp.json` carries richer config than the model represents. It currently treats the surplus as something to drop, never to preserve.

## Proposed fixes

- Add a passthrough / per-harness override for MCP entries that round-trips into the generated manifest (an `oauth` field, or a generic `extra` / `claude` block).
- At minimum, emit a warning when `from_dict` discards unknown keys instead of dropping them silently.

## Workaround

Re-inject the field into the generated `.mcp.json` after `apm install` via a post-install hook, since apm regenerates the file from `apm.yml` on every run.

issues.title: [BUG] Plugin .lsp.json with lspServers wrapper key is silently skipped during install
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

When a marketplace plugin has a `.lsp.json` file using the standard `{ "lspServers": { ... } }` format (as used by Claude Code and Copilot CLI), `apm install` silently skips all LSP servers from that plugin with a misleading error. The plugin's skill files install fine, but the LSP server never makes it into `.github/lsp.json`.

## To Reproduce

1. Create a plugin with a `.lsp.json` in the standard format:

```json
{
  "lspServers": {
    "my-lsp-server": {
      "command": "my-lsp",
      "args": ["--stdio"],
      "extensionToLanguage": {
        ".ext": "mylang"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

2. Add the plugin as a dependency in apm.yml
3. Run apm install

## Expected behavior

my-lsp-server is registered and written to lsp.json.

## Actual behavior

```
Skipping invalid LSP server 'lspServers' from plugin 'my-plugin': LSP dependency 'lspServers' requires 'command'
```

The LSP server is not written anywhere. No other error or indication that something went wrong.

Logs

```text
[+] my-plugin (local)
[!] Skipping invalid LSP server 'lspServers' from plugin 'my-plugin': LSP dependency 'lspServers' requires 'command'
  |-- Skill integrated -> .agents/skills/
  |-- 1 skill(s) integrated -> .agents/skills/
```

## Environment

OS: Windows
APM Version: 0.18.0
Python Version: 3.x

issues.title: [BUG] `apm install` rewrites `apm.lock.yaml` on every run when project has local `.apm/instructions/` + remote APM dep
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

`apm install` unconditionally rewrites `apm.lock.yaml` on every run, updating only the `generated_at` timestamp, when the project has **both** a local `.apm/instructions/` directory **and** at least one remote APM dependency. No files have changed — remote deps report `(files unchanged)` — but the lockfile is always dirtied.

This is the third instance of the same pattern:
- Previously fixed for remote APM deps in [PR #456](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/pull/456) (closes [#450](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/450))
- Previously fixed for MCP deps in [PR #1568](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/pull/1568) (closes [#1532](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/1532))

The `<project root>` local integration code path appears to unconditionally mark the install as modified, triggering a lockfile rewrite regardless of whether the local file content hashes changed.

## To Reproduce

Minimal reproduction repo: https://github.com/AllySummers/apm-generatedat-repro

The repo contains:
- `apm.yml` with one pinned remote APM dep and one local `.apm/instructions/` file
- `apm.lock.yaml` committed from a clean install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/AllySummers/apm-generatedat-repro
cd apm-generatedat-repro
apm install
git diff apm.lock.yaml
```

The diff will show **only** `generated_at` has changed. Run `apm install` again — it changes again. Every run dirties the lockfile.

### Trigger conditions (bisected)

| Config | Lockfile dirtied? |
|--------|-------------------|
| remote APM dep (files unchanged) + local `.apm/instructions/` | **yes** |
| local `.apm/instructions/` only (no remote deps) | no |
| remote APM dep only (no local instructions) | no |
| MCP server (already configured) + local `.apm/instructions/` | no |

The bug **requires both** a remote APM dep and a local instructions directory.

## Expected behavior

When no files have changed, `apm install` should be a no-op:

```
[i] No changes -- install state already up to date in 0.4s.
```

`git diff apm.lock.yaml` should produce an empty diff.

## Actual behavior

`apm install` output:

```
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
[i] Targets: claude, copilot, cursor  (source: apm.yml)
  [+] github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/skills/react-best-practices#4ec6f84b (cached)
  |-- (files unchanged)
  [+] <project root> (local)
  |-- 2 rule(s) integrated (1 adopted) -> 3 targets

[*] Installed 1 APM dependency in 0.4s.
```

`git diff apm.lock.yaml` (only `generated_at` changes, everything else is identical):

```diff
-generated_at: '2026-06-09T03:54:35.441602+00:00'
+generated_at: '2026-06-09T03:54:54.674005+00:00'
```

Note: `[*] Installed 1 APM dependency in 0.4s.` — the "1" counted here is the local `<project root>` entry, not the remote dep (which correctly reported `files unchanged`).

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5.1
- Python Version: 3.14.5
- APM Version: 0.18.0 (c393f33)

## Additional context

The `apm.yml` for the minimal repro:

```yaml
name: apm-generatedat-repro
version: 1.0.0

targets:
  - cursor
  - claude
  - copilot

dependencies:
  apm:
    - vercel-labs/agent-skills/skills/react-best-practices#4ec6f84b61cd3c931046c3e6e398f3ae7de372f7
```

The single `.apm/instructions/coding-conventions.instructions.md`:

```markdown
---
description: General coding conventions
applyTo: 'src/**/*.ts'
---

All TypeScript files must:

- Use named exports (not default exports) for consistency.
- Validate external input with Zod before using it.
- Prefer `const` over `let`; never use `var`.
- Use `async`/`await` over raw Promise chains.
```

---
*This issue was filed with AI assistance.*

issues.title: `.agents/skills/` deployed content escapes drift check + lockfile integrity (silent drift)
issues.body:
## Summary

Committed deployed content under `.agents/skills/**` can silently drift from its `packages/**` (and `.apm/**`) source without any CI gate catching it. Discovered while fixing #1712 / via PR #1714.

## Evidence

- `.agents/skills/apm-review-panel/SKILL.md` on `main` was **415 lines vs 446 in `packages/apm-review-panel/SKILL.md`** — missing the entire `performance-expert` persona (and the matching `panelist-return-schema.json` enum/description). It was last deployed in release commit `6aceef72` (v0.12.4) and never re-synced, yet `main` is green.

## Why nothing catches it (three independent gaps)

1. **`apm audit --ci --no-drift`** in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (job `apm-self-check`) explicitly **disables the install-replay drift comparison** — the only check that would deploy `packages/` and diff against the committed tree.
2. **Lockfile content-integrity does not cover `.agents/skills/`.** The committed `apm.lock.yaml` is a **copilot-target** lockfile: every `deployed_files` entry points to `copilot-app-db://workflows/...`. There is no `.agents/skills/...` path and no `deployed_file_hashes` block, so the SHA-256 integrity check never hashes those files. Running `apm install --target agent-skills` produces a *different* lockfile whose `deployed_files` point at `.agents/skills/...` — confirming the committed lockfile simply tracks a different target than the committed deployed tree.
3. **Gate B git-status drift fallback watches only `.github/ .claude/ .cursor/ .opencode/`** — `.agents/` is **not** in the watch list, and no `apm install` runs in that job anyway, so it is a guaranteed no-op.

## Root-cause questions to answer

- Should the committed lockfile's content-integrity manifest cover **every** committed deploy target (including `.agents/skills/`), not just the single target it was last generated for? Today a repo that deploys to multiple targets but commits a single-target lockfile has unprotected trees.
- Should the CI self-check run a drift gate that is target-aware (i.e. detect that a committed deployed tree no longer matches source) instead of `--no-drift`?
- Should Gate B's git-status watch list include `.agents/`?
- Is the lockfile *supposed* to be single-target, and the `.agents/skills/` tree therefore an unmanaged artifact? If so, that should be explicit, not accidental.

## Acceptance

A reproduction test that: takes a repo with a committed `.agents/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`, mutates source in `packages/<skill>/`, runs the documented CI audit gate, and asserts the gate **fails** on the resulting drift. Plus a decision + fix on which of the three gaps to close.

Found via PR #1714 (the deployed copy was re-synced there as a stopgap; the lockfile was deliberately left untouched to preserve evidence for this investigation).

issues.title: [BUG] Using `--target` with multiple harnesses including Copilot ignores Copilot as a target

E.g. `apm install ... --target claude,copilot` only installs for Claude Code. issues.title: Add --add flag to preserve existing skills during install
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Every time I run `apm install` with a `--skill` flag, it removes previously 
installed skills from the target directory. This makes it impossible to 
build up a set of skills incrementally - each new install silently wipes 
out everything that was installed before.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add an `--add` flag that installs a skill additively, without removing 
existing skills in the target directory.

Example workflow that should work:
apm install repo.git --skill grill-me --target claude
apm install repo.git --skill qa --target claude --add
← both grill-me AND qa should now be present

Without `--add`, the current behavior removes grill-me when qa is installed.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Declaring all skills upfront in apm.yml works as a workaround, but it 
defeats the purpose of having a CLI -sometimes you just want to quickly 
add one more skill without editing a config file.

**Additional context**
This behavior is especially surprising because most package managers 
(npm, pip, cargo) are additive by default -installing a new package 
never removes existing ones. APM doing the opposite is unintuitive and 
easy to miss, since there's no warning when skills are deleted.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Generate a skill for prompt entries when targeting Codex
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

apm supports a `prompt` primitive, which is compiled into a slash command for Claude Code. Codex has no equivalent concept, so apm currently ignores `prompt` entries when targeting Codex.

As a result, any apm package that ships functionality as a `prompt` is effectively unusable on Codex: the author's intent is silently dropped, and a Codex user has no way to invoke that behaviour.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

When targeting Codex, generate a skill for each `prompt` entry instead of ignoring it.

A skill can be invoked explicitly on Codex, so the package author's functionality stays reachable. To reduce the risk of the model running the command on its own, the generated skill `description` can state that it should be invoked only when the user explicitly asks for it (for example: `Invoke only when the user explicitly asks for it.`).

This keeps existing `prompt`-based packages working across both Claude Code and Codex without changing the package format.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **Keep ignoring `prompt` on Codex (current behaviour).** Packages that rely on `prompt` remain broken for Codex users, with no signal to the author.
- **Wait for native command/prompt support in Codex.** If Codex gains an explicit command or prompt mechanism, a future apm version can map `prompt` onto it directly. Until then, generating a skill is a working stopgap, and the migration path stays open.

**Additional context**

Generating a skill is meant as a compatibility shim, not the long-term target. The skill `description` is the main lever for controlling auto-invocation, so its wording matters and may need tuning.

issues.title: Let authors target native context files (root or nested CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md), not just .claude/rules
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

A package author cannot choose where compiled guidance lands on the destination axis: the harness's native context file (`CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`, root or nested in a subdirectory) versus a path-scoped rule file (`.claude/rules/`). Every `instructions` primitive compiles to a rule file. For Claude that is `.claude/rules/<name>.md`, with `applyTo:` translated to `paths:`, and the instructions section is then deduplicated out of `CLAUDE.md`. So for Claude, instruction content can only ever become a path-scoped rule.

These placements behave differently, and both native forms are useful:

- `.claude/rules/<name>.md` with `paths:` is path-scoped and lazily loaded. Claude pulls it in only when it touches a matching file.
- A root `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` is always-on. It stays in context on every turn, and Claude re-injects it after `/compact`.
- A nested `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` (placed in a subdirectory) is the agent-native directory-scoping mechanism. Every major agent loads it when working anywhere in that subtree, and it survives the same way the root file does. This is directory scoping, distinct from the glob and extension scoping of a `paths:` rule.

Three use cases are blocked:

1. **Root, always-on.** Short cross-cutting rules an agent benefits from on every turn (tool-selection conventions, repo-wide layout, "use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations"). `applyTo: "**/*"` does not help: it still compiles to a rule file and is still deduplicated out of the root file.
2. **Nested, directory-scoped.** Guidance that should hold across a whole subtree (a service or package directory) and load whenever the agent works anywhere under it. The agent-native nested context file fits this exactly, but APM never targets it for Claude. The content is forced into a `paths:`-globbed rule instead.
3. **Troubleshooting and diagnostic sessions, no file editing.** A support-engineer agent diagnosing live infrastructure (database health, operator state, cluster logs) never opens a source file, so a `paths:`-globbed rule in `.claude/rules/` never fires and the skill trigger it carries is never seen. The guidance and its skill triggers must be always-on in `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` to be reachable at all. APM can ship the troubleshooting skills, but it cannot place their triggers where a non-editing session will load them. See [IldarMinaev/engineer-workspace](https://github.com/IldarMinaev/engineer-workspace), which deploys PostgreSQL, Patroni, and Kubernetes diagnostic skills through APM for read-only support work of this kind.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A primitive distinct from `instructions`, provisionally `agentsmd` (or `context-file`), whose contract is "this content belongs in the harness's native context file," with an author-declared destination directory.

- The author declares a preferred folder (for example `dir: "."` for the root file, or `dir: "services/payments"` for a nested one), and APM writes the content into that directory's `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`.
- On Claude the content lands in the chosen `CLAUDE.md` and is exempt from the `.claude/rules/` deduplication. It is meant to live in the context file, so the dedup pass must leave it there.
- On harnesses that already fold instructions into a context file (`AGENTS.md` for Codex and OpenCode, `GEMINI.md`), the primitive maps onto the existing context-file path; nested directories use that harness's nested-`AGENTS.md` convention.
- The difference from `instructions` is the destination (a native context file, root or nested), not the scoping strategy. `--single-agents` collapses nested files into the root, as it does today.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **`apm compile --no-dedup` / `--force-instructions`.** This keeps the instructions section in `CLAUDE.md`, but it is a consumer-side, all-or-nothing flag rather than a per-primitive author declaration, and it duplicates content into both `.claude/rules/` and the context file. That is the opposite of choosing a single destination.
- **`applyTo:` distributed placement.** APM already places nested `AGENTS.md` for fold-into-root targets via `applyTo:`, but for Claude the matching content is deduplicated out of the nested `CLAUDE.md` and only the rule file survives. The nested-context-file path is reachable for Codex, Gemini, and OpenCode, but not for Claude. That is exactly the gap.
- **Spec Kit constitution.** The constitution block is always written to the top of `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`, so it covers always-on root content. But it is a single project-level block tied to `memory/constitution.md`, not a reusable primitive an upstream package can ship through `apm dependencies`, and it has no nested form.
- **Path-scoped rules alone.** Glob scoping is correct for "true when editing X." It is the wrong tool for always-on rules and for whole-subtree rules, and it is not re-injected after `/compact` the way a context file is.

**Additional context**

The motivating case is a large monorepo consuming platform conventions through `apm dependencies`. A few cross-cutting rules belong always-on in the root file, per-service conventions belong in that service's nested `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`, and stack-specific how-tos stay in path-scoped rules and skills. Today only the last is expressible for Claude.

Path scoping also assumes the agent reaches a matching file. Read-only sessions such as incident triage, infrastructure diagnostics, and support work break that assumption: there is no file event to trigger a `paths:` rule, so any guidance gated behind one stays unreachable. That guidance has to live in the always-on context file.

Relevant current behaviour:

- the Claude-Code deduplication that omits the instructions section from `CLAUDE.md` (`apm compile --target claude`, docs `producer/compile.md`, closes #1138 / #1146);
- distributed placement driven by `applyTo:` (`concepts/primitives-and-targets.md`, "Where compiled context files land");
- the compatibility matrix where `instructions / claude = native` resolves to `.claude/rules/<name>.md`.

issues.title: [BUG]  apm pack marketplace resolution ignores {name}, pins every package to the highest global version tag
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When `apm pack` builds a `marketplace.json`, the version-range resolution ignores the `{name}` placeholder in the tag pattern. Every remote package entry that uses a semver range is resolved to the **single highest `{version}` tag across the whole repository**, regardless of the package name. As a result,all entries end up pinned to the same `ref`/`sha` instead of each resolving to its own `{name}-v{version}` tag.

In a monorepo marketplace where each package is tagged independently as `{name}-v{version}`, this makes per-package resolution unusable: the produced `marketplace.json` points every plugin at one unrelated package's tag.

A clue that the package name is not threaded into the resolver: in `--offline` mode the error names an**empty** package — `Offline mode: no cached refs for '<owner>/<repo>' (package '')`.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create a marketplace `apm.yml` with two packages from the same remote repo, each pinned by a semver**range**, using a name-scoped tag pattern:

   ```yaml
   name: my-marketplace
   version: 1.0.0
   description: repro
   marketplace:
     owner:
       name: Acme
       url: https://github.com/acme/catalog
     build:
       tagPattern: "{name}-v{version}"
     versioning:
       strategy: tag_pattern
     outputs:
       claude: {}
     packages:
       - name: pkg-a
         source: acme/catalog
         subdir: packages/pkg-a
         version: "^1.0.0"
       - name: pkg-b
         source: acme/catalog
         subdir: packages/pkg-b
         version: "^1.0.0"
   ```

2. On `acme/catalog`, create per-package tags at different versions:
   - `pkg-a-v1.0.0`
   - `pkg-b-v2.0.0`

3. Run:
   ```bash
   apm pack -m claude
   ```

4. Inspect the generated `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`:
   ```bash
   jq -r '.plugins[] | "\(.name)\t\(.source.ref)"' .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
   ```

   Observed output — both entries resolve to the highest global version tag (`pkg-b-v2.0.0`), name ignored:
   ```
   pkg-a    pkg-b-v2.0.0
   pkg-b    pkg-b-v2.0.0
   ```

**Expected behavior**

Each entry should resolve against its **own** `{name}-v{version}` tags only, picking the highest tag that satisfies that entry's range:

```
pkg-a    pkg-a-v1.0.0
pkg-b    pkg-b-v2.0.0
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows (MINGW64 / Git Bash); also reproduced conceptually independent of OS
 - Python Version: 3.12.10
 - APM Version: 0.20.0
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): n/a

**Additional context**

Variations tested — none restore name-scoped resolution:

| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| `build.tagPattern: "{name}-v{version}"` (single dash) + semver range | All entries → highest global version tag |
| `build.tagPattern: "{name}--v{version}"` (double dash, canonical convention) + matching tags | Same collapse |
| Per-package `tag_pattern: "{name}--v{version}"` on each entry | Same collapse |
| `versioning.strategy: per_package` + per-package `tag_pattern` | Same collapse |
| Exact `version: "1.2.1"` (bare version) | Resolves by **version only** — picks the alphabetically-first tag with that version, still ignoring `{name}`. Only "works" when the version is unique to one package or that package happens to be alphabetically first. |
| `version: "pkg-a-v1.0.0"` (full tag in `version:`) | Errors: `No tag matching version 'pkg-a-v1.0.0'found ... (pattern='{name}-v{version}')` |
| **`ref: "pkg-a-v1.0.0"` (full tag in `ref:`)** | **Correct** — resolves each entry to its own tag (this is the only working path, but it forces pinning immutable refs in `apm.yml` and writes the annotated-tag-object SHA rather than the commit SHA) |

Summary: the documented semantics (manifest schema: *"the resolver lists git tags matching the `{name}--v{version}` convention, filters to those satisfying the constraint, and resolves to the highest matching tag"*) are not honored — the `{name}` component is dropped and resolution falls back to a global version match. The only correct path today is the `ref:` override, which defeats the purpose of semver-range marketplace resolution in a monorepo.

issues.title: [BUG] Regression: #288/#290 - Docs no longer cover what to commit
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The [quick start documentation](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/quickstart/) used to have a section clearly explaining which files should and should not be committed. The previous guidance was:

```markdown
**What to commit:**
- `apm.yml` and `apm.lock.yaml` — version-controlled, shared with the team.
- `.github/` deployed files (`prompts/`, `agents/`, `instructions/`, `skills/`, `hooks/`) — commit them so every contributor (and [Copilot on github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot)) gets agent context immediately after cloning, before they run `apm install` to sync and regenerate files.
- `.claude/` deployed files (`agents/`, `commands/`, `skills/`, `hooks/`) — same rationale for Claude Code users: committed files give instant context on clone, while `apm install` remains the way to refresh them from `apm.yml`.
- `apm_modules/` — add to `.gitignore`. Rebuilt from the lockfile on install.

:::tip[Keeping deployed files in sync]
When you update `apm.yml`, re-run `apm install` and commit the changed `.github/` and `.claude/` files. A [CI drift check](../../integrations/ci-cd/#verify-deployed-primitives) catches stale files automatically.
```

This was added from issue #288 / PR #290.

The quick start documentation [moved around starting on May 11, 2026](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/commits/main/docs/src/content/docs/quickstart.mdx) (PR #1252) and the section on what you should/shouldn't commit has been lost entirely from the documentation.

The only place I can find it now is hidden [down in an APM usage guide skill](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/feab133330f87bea06ec1d6ab23e1fb9d04e3e59/packages/apm-guide/.apm/skills/apm-usage/workflow.md?plain=1#L93).

My team and I were having a discussion recently about whether or not installed/compiled artifacts like `.github/instructions` or `.claude/rules` should be committed and I tried to refer my team to the docs only to find the docs gone. (I remember, though, that previously this guidance was somewhat hard to find anyway - it's not in the README, it wasn't anywhere but the quick start.)

It would be good to put the "what to ignore, what to commit" docs back, possibly in a more visible place - maybe both during setup _and_ at some point in the overall workflow docs so people following the workflow have more complete guidance.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Enhance apm.lock.yaml to Include Installed Package Name and Version Metadata
issues.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

APM packages require a `name` and `version` in `apm.yml`, but after `apm install` consumers cannot easily determine which package versions are installed because `apm.lock.yaml` only records repository, path, commit, and hash information.

This becomes more challenging when packages have transitive dependencies. For example, installing a Spring Boot package may automatically install additional packages such as Mermaid, documentation standards, or other shared packages. While these dependencies appear in `apm.lock.yaml`, their package versions are not visible.

As a result, it is difficult to answer:

* Which version of the Spring Boot package is installed?
* Which versions of transitive dependencies were installed?
* Which repositories are using older package versions?
* What changed between two package upgrades?

### Describe the solution you'd like

Enhance `apm.lock.yaml` to include package metadata extracted from each package's `apm.yml`, such as package name and version.

Example:

```yaml
dependencies:
  - name: springboot
    version: 1.2.2
    resolved_commit: b62358...
    virtual_path: packages/springboot

  - name: mermaid
    version: 1.0.4
    resolved_commit: b62358...
    virtual_path: packages/mermaid

  - name: documentations
    version: 2.1.0
    resolved_commit: b62358...
    virtual_path: packages/documentations
```

Ideally this information should be available for both direct and transitive dependencies.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Generating a custom inventory file by parsing `apm.lock.yaml` and then reading each package's `apm.yml` to determine the package version. While this works, it requires additional scripts and custom tooling in every consuming repository.

### Additional context

Our organization maintains shared APM packages such as Spring Boot, Angular, Mermaid, and documentation standards. Developers often need to understand exactly which package versions are installed in a repository, including automatically installed dependencies.

Having package name and version information directly available in `apm.lock.yaml` would make dependency inventory, auditing, troubleshooting, and upgrade planning much easier while preserving the existing commit-based lockfile behavior.

issues.title: [DESIGN] Per-package primitive routing (`targets:`) as the single placement mechanism
issues.body:
## North star

APM needs exactly **one** answer to "who controls which primitive goes to which harness, and in what shape." This issue records the converged three-layer model so future requests (and PRs) resolve against a single design instead of accreting per-type flags and new verbs.

This supersedes the per-primitive-type approach in #1898 and is the design that PR #1902 implements.

## The three layers

| Layer | Question | Mechanism | Status |
|-------|----------|-----------|--------|
| **CONSENT** | May this package's executable run at all? | `executables: {allow, deny}` keyed per-package x per-exec-type (hooks/mcp/bin/canvas), deny-wins, deny-by-default | shipped (`security/executables.py`) |
| **PLACEMENT** | Which harness(es) does this package go to? | per-package `targets:` on a dependency entry, **uniform across every primitive type in that package** | PR #1902 |
| **PORTING** | What shape per harness? | each primitive written to the harness's native format (`.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.agents/skills/`, ...) | shipped |
| *(intra-harness)* | Where inside a harness do instructions land? | `apm compile` (root/nested `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules` toggle) | shipped |

## Design rulings (and why)

1. **No new lifecycle verb.** `apm install` is idempotent regeneration; `apm audit` detects drift. We do not add `apm sync`, `apm mcp export`, or a `--check` flag (declines #1868 / closes PR #1905).
2. **No per-primitive-TYPE routing for inert primitives** (declines #1898). Splitting one package's skills to one harness and its instructions to another is a *fork* of that package. The supported path is per-package routing: route an instruction-only package to one harness and a skill-only package to another. The bloat #1898 describes is a harness-standards gap (Claude does not read the `.agents/skills/` convention that Copilot/Cursor/Codex/Gemini share), not an APM defect.
3. **Hooks are not special.** "hooks off" = the CONSENT trust floor (`apm deny <pkg> hooks`). "hooks to one harness" = plain per-package `targets:`. No dedicated `hooks:` lever.
4. **We port, we do not glue.** Porting a primitive into each harness's native format is faithful porting. Inventing a universal cross-harness format, or translating semantics between harnesses that disagree on a should-be-standard, is out of scope. (This is also why #1892 is a porting *bug*, not a translation layer.)

## Folds into this design

- #1898 -- per-package routing covers the legit residual; per-type filter declined.
- #1868 / PR #1905 -- export verb declined.
- #1894 -- already expressible via the deny-by-default trust floor; at most a `--no-hooks` sugar that writes the `deny`.
- #1807 -- intra-harness placement served by `apm compile`; any author-intent residual is the PORTING layer here.
- #1892 -- the porting bug PR #1902 fixes.

## Implementation

The build surface is substantially PR #1902. Re-reviewed via the apm-review-panel against this model, then driven to green. #1882 (require explicit targets) is tracked separately as opt-in governance.
