**Additional context**
This behavior felt a bit like a gotcha, the dependency was specified in some upstream reusable package, but it was rather opaque that this behavior was happening.

This isn't the first time this automagic inference of the type of repo has bit me when setting up APM packages. Where the packaging-type specific behavior made certain operations a no-op based on how APM parses the package. (So the `./skill/<skill name>/SKILL.md` file is there, but based on how APM parses the package metadata installing said skill becomes a no-op.)

It's extremely hard for a novice to reason how APM will consume a package, especially when trying to use APM to also point at externally authored dependencies, which are more likely to include unknown packaging standards / formats which aren't actually used by the end-user.

Previously, I ran into https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/2116 (APM seeing  the `.claude-plugin/` config as the authoritative list of skills, hence trying to install skills not mention in the plugin becoming a no-op). 

It makes me wonder if there should be a "dumb" way to install skills, or nudge the user towards a way to bypass the automagic and simply install skills as a plain folder. (From #2116 I remember that the workaround is the alternative install format: `❯ apm install kunchenguid/lavish-axi/skills/lavish --target codex`.)

issues.title: [BUG] User-scope hook deployment leaves out the plugin manifest: scripts reading ../../.claude-plugin/plugin.json crash (Codex Companion plugin)
issues.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #2023. Hook deployment now copies the sibling modules next to a hook entry script, but a plugin whose hook scripts read files *outside* the scripts directory still crashes at runtime, because `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is rewritten to the partial copy under `~/.claude/hooks/<pkg>/` rather than to the full package tree.

Concrete case: `openai/codex-plugin-cc/plugins/codex` (Codex Companion). `hooks/hooks.json` declares

```json
"command": "node \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/stop-review-gate-hook.mjs\""
```

and `scripts/lib/app-server.mjs` does

```js
const PLUGIN_MANIFEST_URL = new URL("../../.claude-plugin/plugin.json", import.meta.url);
const PLUGIN_MANIFEST = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(PLUGIN_MANIFEST_URL, "utf8"));
```

After `apm install -g` the deployed tree is `~/.claude/hooks/codex/scripts/{lib/,*.mjs,package.json}` only. Every Stop / SessionStart / SessionEnd invocation then fails:

```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/Users/<me>/.claude/hooks/codex/.claude-plugin/plugin.json'
    at file:///Users/<me>/.claude/hooks/codex/scripts/lib/app-server.mjs:20:39
```

The same plugin installed natively through Claude Code's plugin system works, because there `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is the whole plugin directory. The plugin also ships `prompts/` and `schemas/` next to `scripts/`, which the review gate reads through the broker.

## Expected

Either of:

1. Rewrite `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` (and `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`) to the package's own directory under `apm_modules/<owner>/<pkg>/…` for user-scope deploys instead of copying scripts into `~/.claude/hooks/<pkg>/`. The full tree already exists there, so every relative read works and nothing is duplicated.
2. If copying stays, copy the plugin manifest (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`) and the package's non-primitive directories alongside the hook scripts, so the deployed root is a faithful plugin root.

## Environment

- apm 0.29.0 from commit `656f3d6e6dbade369b6fc8727a4eb7b164409b6d`
- macOS 15 arm64, target `claude`, user scope
- Workaround in use: copying `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` into `~/.claude/hooks/codex/.claude-plugin/` by hand

issues.title: [BUG] Unix installer implicitly escalates privileges for default installation
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The Unix installer defaults `APM_INSTALL_DIR` to `/usr/local/bin` and derives `/usr/local/lib/apm` for the bundle. When these locations are not writable, the script automatically invokes `sudo` for removal, directory creation, copying, marker creation, and symlink installation.

A routine per-user CLI installation should not implicitly transition into privileged filesystem operations. Supporting an environment-variable override does not make the default unprivileged.

Public source at the inspected revision:
- [Default install directory](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2/install.sh#L25-L28).
- [Privileged installation operations](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2/install.sh#L718-L758).

**To Reproduce**
1. Inspect or exercise `install.sh` in a disposable macOS/Linux environment as an ordinary user, leaving `APM_INSTALL_DIR` and `APM_LIB_DIR` unset.
2. Ensure the default system installation locations are not user-writable. In an automated harness, stub `sudo` to record and reject calls rather than elevating privileges.
3. Reach the installation phase with a valid fixture bundle. The current script attempts privileged operations automatically.

This report is grounded in the source path; no elevated installation is required to demonstrate it.

**Expected behavior**
- Fresh ordinary-user installs default to documented user-owned locations and never invoke `sudo` implicitly.
- Deliberate system-wide installation remains possible through a clearly documented opt-in or administrator-managed procedure. An unwritable destination without that intent produces an actionable nonzero failure.
- Explain PATH requirements accurately without silently rewriting shell profiles.
- Preserve existing path-safety and prior-installation guards.
- Account for existing system-wide/custom installations and `apm self-update`: do not silently create a competing second installation, remove an installation the caller cannot manage, or overwrite a package-manager-owned installation.
- Cover fresh user-local installs, unwritable custom paths, explicit system-wide intent, and existing-installation updates in regression coverage.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
- OS: macOS / Linux (Unix installer).
- Python Version: N/A for the standalone binary path.
- APM Version: v0.29.0 installer; the same installer content was present at main revision `13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2`.
- VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A.

**Logs**
N/A. Source-based report; no user-specific logs are necessary.

**Additional context**
The script is not executed wholesale under `sudo`, and normal APM usage does not inherently require administrator privileges. The defect is automatic privilege escalation during bootstrap. This is distinct from the previously addressed directory-safety problem in #1690. A changed default needs a concise migration note for existing installations.

issues.title: [BUG] apm prune exits zero after orphan deletion failure
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm prune` exits successfully with status code `0` when deletion of an orphaned package fails. The failure is logged, but the command does not retain a failure state. The orphaned package remains on disk.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create a project with an `apm.yml` containing no APM dependencies.
2. Create an orphaned package directory under `apm_modules/`.
3. Make the package directory undeletable, or simulate `safe_rmtree()` raising `OSError`.
4. Run `apm prune`.
5. Check the exit status and confirm that the orphaned package remains.

Observed output includes:

```text
Failed to remove bad-org/bad-repo: permission denied

issues.title: [BUG] Document and align APM_HOME behavior for global user state
issues.body:
## Problem

APM documents `APM_HOME` as an override for user configuration and state.

However, APM 0.29.0 uses `APM_HOME` for lifecycle state while global package commands continue to use `~/.apm`.

The documentation does not explain this difference. It does not define which files, commands, or deployment paths `APM_HOME` controls.

## Current documentation

The [environment-variable reference](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/environment-variables/#cache-and-filesystem) describes `APM_HOME` as:

> Override the APM home directory used for user config and state.

The [`apm lifecycle` reference](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/lifecycle/#environment-variables) defines these paths:

```text
$APM_HOME/apm.yml
$APM_HOME/scripts-trust.json
```

The lifecycle guide also documents the script log under:

```text
$APM_HOME/logs/scripts.log
```

In contrast, the global package-command documentation names `~/.apm` directly:

- [`apm install --global`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/install/#behavior) reads or creates `~/.apm/apm.yml`.
- [`apm update --global`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/update/) operates on dependencies under `~/.apm`.
- [`apm lock --global`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/lock/) writes the user-scope lockfile under `~/.apm`.
- [`apm deps --global`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/deps/) reads modules and lock state under `~/.apm`.

None of those command references explain whether `APM_HOME` changes the documented paths.

## Current implementation

The implementation follows the same split:

- [`core/lifecycle_scripts.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/core/lifecycle_scripts.py) reads the user lifecycle manifest from `$APM_HOME/apm.yml`.
- [`core/script_trust.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/core/script_trust.py) stores lifecycle trust state under `APM_HOME`.
- [`core/scope.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/core/scope.py) resolves global package metadata through `Path.home() / ".apm"`.
- [`config.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/config.py) resolves user configuration through `~/.apm/config.json`.

One APM process can therefore use two different user-manifest paths:

```text
$APM_HOME/apm.yml
~/.apm/apm.yml
```

Lifecycle processing can read the first file while global package commands read the second file.

## Why this matters

A user can set `APM_HOME` to isolate APM during a test, automation run, or temporary experiment:

```console
export APM_HOME=/tmp/apm-test
apm install --global example-org/example-package
```

Based on the [documented description of `APM_HOME`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/environment-variables/#cache-and-filesystem), the user can reasonably expect APM-owned user state to remain under:

```text
/tmp/apm-test
```

The global install can instead read or write:

```text
~/.apm/apm.yml
~/.apm/apm.lock.yaml
~/.apm/apm_modules/
```

Depending on the target, it can also deploy files under the operating-system home.

This behavior can:

- Read the user’s real global manifest instead of the isolated manifest.
- Write package state outside the requested APM directory.
- Make an isolated test depend on existing user configuration.
- Leave test state in the user’s real home.
- Cause lifecycle processing and package installation to read different manifests.

## Documentation gap

The current documentation does not answer these questions:

1. Does `APM_HOME` control all APM-owned user metadata or only lifecycle state?
2. Does it affect global install, update, lock, dependency, and configuration commands?
3. Does it change global deployment destinations?
4. How does it interact with target-specific variables such as `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`?
5. Is `APM_HOME` suitable for isolated tests and temporary global installations?
6. Which path takes precedence when multiple home variables exist?

## Requested outcome

Please define and document one supported contract for `APM_HOME`.

The implementation and documentation must agree on that contract. Several designs appear possible.

### Alternative 1: Use APM_HOME for all APM metadata

Use `APM_HOME` for APM-owned user metadata and configuration:

```text
$APM_HOME/apm.yml
$APM_HOME/apm.lock.yaml
$APM_HOME/apm_modules/
$APM_HOME/config.json
$APM_HOME/scripts-trust.json
$APM_HOME/logs/
```

Global target deployment can continue to use the operating-system home or target-specific overrides.

The documentation must state that `APM_HOME` isolates APM metadata but does not redirect target deployment.

### Alternative 2: Add a global deployment root

Keep `APM_HOME` as the metadata root and add a separate variable, such as `APM_GLOBAL_HOME`, for global deployment.

For example:

```text
APM_HOME=/tmp/apm-metadata
APM_GLOBAL_HOME=/tmp/apm-user
```

APM metadata would use `APM_HOME`. Global target files would use `APM_GLOBAL_HOME`, unless a target-specific variable has higher precedence.

This option supports isolated global installations without changing the process user’s operating-system home.

The documentation must define precedence between:

```text
target-specific override
APM_GLOBAL_HOME
operating-system home
```

### Alternative 3: Document APM_HOME as lifecycle-only

If the current split is intentional, narrow the [`APM_HOME` description](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/environment-variables/#cache-and-filesystem).

For example:

> Override the directory used for user lifecycle manifests, lifecycle trust state, and lifecycle logs.

The global command documentation must then state that dependency and configuration state always remains under `~/.apm`.

A more specific variable name or deprecation path can reduce confusion because `APM_HOME` currently implies broader scope.

## Acceptance criteria

1. One authoritative document defines the exact scope of `APM_HOME`.
2. Global command references state whether `APM_HOME` changes their paths.
3. Documentation lists the paths for manifests, lockfiles, modules, configuration, lifecycle state, and deployment.
4. Documentation defines precedence with target-specific home variables.
5. Documentation includes an isolation example.
6. Tests verify the selected path contract.
7. Lifecycle and global package commands do not silently select different manifests unless the documentation explicitly defines that behavior.

issues.title: [BUG] insteadOf rewrite matching the fetched URL blocks private installs since 0.30.0
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Since 0.30.0, `apm install` cannot download a **private** git dependency when the user's git config holds an `insteadOf` rewrite rule that matches the URL apm fetches:

```
Failed to download dependency OWNER/REPO: Unable to verify Git URL rewrite safety
(Git URL-match probe failed); check Git configuration and retry; inspect matching
rules with 'git config --show-origin --get-regexp ^url\..*\.insteadOf$' and remove
the unsafe rule
```

The rule is the most common SSH-preferring setup there is:

```
url."git@github.com:".insteadOf = https://github.com/
```

0.29.0 installs the same dependency in the same conditions without error, so this is a 0.30.0 regression.

**To Reproduce**

1. `git config --global url."git@github.com:".insteadOf https://github.com/`
2. In an empty directory, write an `apm.yml` declaring one **private** git dependency
3. `apm install`

Result: fails as above on 0.30.0, succeeds on 0.29.0.

Three observations that narrow the trigger:

- **Only the authenticated retry path.** The debug log shows `Unauthenticated access failed for github.com; will retry with [REDACTED]` immediately before the failure, so a public dependency never reaches the probe.
- **Only a rule that matches the fetched URL.** With `url."git@example.com:".insteadOf = https://example.com/` — same rule shape, different host — the install succeeds. Neither SSH nor the mere existence of a rewrite is the trigger.
- **Only when something must actually be downloaded.** In a project whose lockfile and `apm_modules/` are already populated, both `apm install` and `apm update --dry-run` succeed on 0.30.0.

**Expected behavior**

A standard `insteadOf` rule redirecting GitHub HTTPS to SSH should not prevent installing a private dependency. If a rewrite genuinely cannot be validated, the message should state what was probed and why it failed, rather than asking the user to remove a legitimate and widespread configuration.

**Environment**

- OS: Windows 11 Pro (26200)
- Python: 3.12 (bundled in the release binary)
- APM: 0.30.0 — works on 0.29.0
- git: 2.55.0.windows.5

**Logs**

```
[>] Resolving PKG...
DEBUG apm_cli.core.auth Unauthenticated access failed for github.com; will retry with [REDACTED]
  [x] 1 package failed:
    +- PKG -- Failed to download dependency OWNER/REPO: Unable to verify Git URL
       rewrite safety (Git URL-match probe failed); ...
[x] Installation failed with 1 error(s) in 0.3s. No install transaction changes were committed.
```

**Additional context**

`src/apm_cli/utils/git_env.py` grows from 113 lines in v0.29.0 to 1524 in v0.30.0, and neither `GitUrlRewriteProbeError` nor `--get-urlmatch` appears anywhere in the v0.29.0 tree. The commits in range that introduce the mechanism are `7da6ebe9` (`fix: bind Git execution to validated policy`), `b33b313c` (`fix: close Git transport policy gaps`) and `129b6bc2` (`fix: close final Git transport gaps`).

The raised error is the `Git URL-match probe failed` branch of `_urlmatched_header_group`, i.e. `git config --null --get-urlmatch http.extraHeader <url>` returning something other than 0 or 1. We could not reproduce a non-zero exit by hand: run from the git executable's directory, with `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` / `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` pointed at devnull and an injected `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0` header, that command exits 0 — with both `/dev/null` and `nul` as the devnull path. So the failing input is something in apm's own probe environment that is not observable from outside.

Worth noting: the machine's git config declares no `http.extraHeader` of its own, so the header group the probe inspects can only come from the credential apm injects on the authenticated retry.

issues.title: [BUG] git+path dep validates apm.yml at sparse subdir, not repo root
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm install` fails for a `git:` + `path:` object-form dependency when `path` points at a plain subdirectory that is **not itself an installable package** (no `apm.yml`, `SKILL.md`, or `plugin.json` at that subpath) but is part of a larger package whose manifest lives at the true repository root, one or more levels above `path`.

Resolution correctly identifies the repository and performs a sparse checkout of just `path`. But package-structure validation then runs `apm.yml`/`SKILL.md`/`plugin.json` discovery against that same sparse-checkout leaf directory instead of the repository root, so it never finds the manifest — even though the manifest genuinely exists in the repo, just above the checked-out subtree. The install aborts, no `apm.lock.yaml` is written, and (as a downstream consequence) `apm pack` on the same project silently produces a bundle containing only a synthesized `plugin.json` with no dependency content, since `pack` only collects files recorded as `deployed_files` in a lockfile that was never created.

This is distinct from #382 (fixed: invalid clone URL construction on generic hosts) and #2066 (fixed: missing CLI shorthand for GitLab subpaths) — in this report, the object form is used directly and the correct repository is cloned. It's also distinct from #2888 (`skills:` subset validating the wrong root) in that the target subdirectory here isn't a skill or package fragment at all — it's a shared folder (e.g. `scripts/`, `docs/`) that is only ever meant to be consumed alongside its sibling manifest, not as a standalone unit.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create (or use an existing) self-hosted GitLab repository with this layout at its root:

   ```
   my-repo/
     apm.yml
     scripts/
       foo.py
     references/
       bar.md
   ```

   `apm.yml`:

   ```yaml
   name: my-package
   version: 1.0.0
   description: example package with shared subdirectories
   type: skill
   dependencies:
     apm: []
   ```

2. In a **separate** consumer project, add object-form dependencies pointing at the two subdirectories:

   ```yaml
   # apm.yml
   name: consumer
   version: 1.0.0
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - git: https://gitlab.example.com/my-org/my-repo.git
         type: gitlab
         path: scripts
       - git: https://gitlab.example.com/my-org/my-repo.git
         type: gitlab
         path: references
   ```

3. Run:

   ```
   apm install -v
   ```

4. See error:

   ```
   [>] Resolving my-package-scripts...
   [>] Resolving my-package-references...
     [i] perf: subdir gitlab.example.com/my-org/my-repo/references cache=shared-bare sparse=references
     [i] perf: bare clone strategy=--depth=1 --branch <default> took=1244ms
     [i] perf: subdir gitlab.example.com/my-org/my-repo/scripts cache=shared-bare sparse=scripts
     [i] perf: bare clone strategy=--depth=1 --branch <default> took=577ms
   Failed to download dependency my-org/my-repo: Invalid APM package my-org/my-repo:
   - Not a valid APM package: no apm.yml, SKILL.md, or plugin structure found in <hash>.
     Ensure the package has SKILL.md (skill bundle), apm.yml + .apm/ (APM package), or plugin.json (Claude plugin) at its root.
   [x] Installation failed with 2 error(s). No install transaction changes were committed.
   ```

5. As a downstream consequence, `apm pack` (no lockfile present) still exits 0 but emits only:

   ```
   build/my-package-1.0.0/plugin.json
   ```

   with none of the dependency content, and no warning that the bundle is effectively empty of dependency files.

6. Installing that resulting bundle elsewhere then warns:

   ```
   Bundle has no apm.lock.yaml
   ```

**Expected behavior**

When a git dependency uses the object form with an explicit `path:`, APM should validate package structure (`apm.yml` / `SKILL.md` / `plugin.json` discovery) against the **repository root** first. If the repo root is a valid APM package, the `path:` subdirectory should be treated as a slice of that package's content to install (similar to how `skills:` subset installs are meant to work per #2888, or how local/transitive relative-path deps are anchored per #857), not as a standalone package that must itself carry a manifest.

At minimum, if this scenario is genuinely unsupported today, `apm install` should surface an actionable error explaining that `path:` values must point at a directory containing their own manifest, rather than the generic "not a valid APM package" message — and `apm pack` should fail loudly (or warn prominently) instead of silently emitting a near-empty bundle when the lockfile it depends on for content collection doesn't exist.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: macOS
- Python Version: 3.12 (via installed `apm` binary)
- APM Version: 0.30.0 (08e85c4e42)
- VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A

**Logs**

Verbose `apm install` output (paths/hostnames anonymized, otherwise unmodified):

```
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
Parsed apm.yml: 2 APM deps, 0 MCP deps
[>] Resolving my-package-scripts...
[>] Resolving my-package-references...
  [i] gitlab.example.com -- token from git-credential-fill
    [i] perf: subdir gitlab.example.com/my-org/my-repo/references cache=shared-bare sparse=references
    [i] perf: bare clone strategy=--depth=1 --branch <default> took=1244ms
    [i] perf: subdir gitlab.example.com/my-org/my-repo/scripts cache=shared-bare sparse=scripts
    [i] perf: bare clone strategy=--depth=1 --branch <default> took=577ms
    [i] perf: materialize sparse=yes size=0.60 MB
    [i] perf: materialize sparse=yes size=0.75 MB
  Failed to download dependency my-org/my-repo: Invalid APM package my-org/my-repo:
  - Not a valid APM package: no apm.yml, SKILL.md, or plugin structure found in <hash-1>.
    Ensure the package has SKILL.md (skill bundle), apm.yml + .apm/ (APM package), or plugin.json (Claude plugin) at its root.
  Failed to download dependency my-org/my-repo: Invalid APM package my-org/my-repo:
  - Not a valid APM package: no apm.yml, SKILL.md, or plugin structure found in <hash-2>.
    Ensure the package has SKILL.md (skill bundle), apm.yml + .apm/ (APM package), or plugin.json (Claude plugin) at its root.
Resolved 2 direct dependencies (no transitive)
Phase: resolve -> 3.412s
[x] 2 packages failed:
  +- my-package-scripts -- Failed to download dependency my-org/my-repo: Invalid APM package ...
  +- my-package-references -- Failed to download dependency my-org/my-repo: Invalid APM package ...
[x] Installation failed with 2 error(s) in 3.7s. No install transaction changes were committed.
```

**Additional context**

- Traced to `apm_cli/deps/package_validator.py::validate_package_structure`, which does `apm_yml = package_path / "apm.yml"` where `package_path` is the sparse-checkout leaf (the `path:` subdirectory), not the repository root that was actually cloned.
- The clone itself is correct: `apm_cli` resolves the right repo, correctly splits `repo_url` vs. `path` for this self-hosted GitLab host (confirmed via `GITLAB_HOST`/`is_gitlab_hostname` classification working as intended), and performs a sparse `git sparse-checkout set <path>` against it. The bug is purely in what gets validated afterward.
- Moving the subdirectory content under `.apm/` (e.g. `.apm/scripts/`, per the package-authoring docs) does **not** help — `validate_package_structure` fails at the very first `apm.yml`-existence check, before any `.apm/` content is even inspected, because `package_path` is wrong regardless of what's inside it.
- Workaround: give each `path:` subdirectory its own standalone `apm.yml` (and, if applicable, `.apm/`), duplicating package identity across every subpath in the same repo. This works but is not a documented pattern and creates multiple independent "packages" for what is conceptually one package with shared subdirectories.
- Related (not duplicates):
  - #382 — different bug (bad clone URL on generic hosts), already fixed.
  - #2066 — different bug (missing shorthand syntax), already fixed.
  - #1014 — different bug (API vs. git clone for GitLab), already fixed; confirmed git clone now works correctly.
  - #872, #1571 — monorepo / shared-package resolution, but for cases where the subpath **is** itself a skill or the dependency type is `local`, not remote `git`+`path`.
  - #2888 — same class of bug (sparse materialization validated at the wrong root) but for the `skills:` subset field on skill bundles, not `path:` on arbitrary non-package subdirectories.

issues.title: [BUG] GitLab sparse-fetch rewrites ssh:// URL with custom port to HTTPS on same host
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a `type: gitlab` dependency uses an `ssh://` URL with a non-standard port (e.g. `ssh://git@gitlab-ssh.example.com:2222/...`), the git sparse-fetch path constructs a remote URL using HTTPS against the same hostname. For GitLab instances where the SSH host alias differs from the web endpoint, this causes the git transport to speak TLS to an SSH-only host, then silently fall back to the GitLab REST API (which also fails because it reuses the SSH port with HTTPS).

**To Reproduce**

1. Host: self-hosted GitLab at `gitlab.example.com:443` (HTTPS web) with SSH-only alias at `gitlab-ssh.example.com:2222`
2. apm.yml:
   ```yaml
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - git: ssh://git@gitlab-ssh.example.com:2222/owner/repo.git
         path: agents/some-agent.agent.md
         type: gitlab
   ```
3. Run `apm install`

**Observed result**
```
HTTPSConnectionPool(host='gitlab-ssh.example.com', port=2222):
Max retries exceeded with url: /api/v4/projects/owner%2Frepo/repository/files/...
(Caused by SSLError(SSLError(1, '[SSL: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER] wrong version number')))
```

With `APM_DEBUG=1`:
```
[DEBUG] git sparse fetch: host=gitlab-ssh.example.com repo=owner/repo ref=main paths=1
[DEBUG] git transport unavailable for gitlab-ssh.example.com/owner/repo; falling back to GitLab REST API (GitFileTransportError)
```

`strace` confirms the sparse-fetch worktree used `git remote add origin https://gitlab-ssh.example.com/...` and invoked `git-remote-https`. The SSH URL and custom port were lost.

**Expected behavior**

The original SSH URL and port should be preserved for the git transport remote URL. A `git ls-remote` over the same `ssh://` URL with port 2222 succeeds from the same environment.

**Environment:**
 - OS: Linux (container)
 - APM Version: 0.30.0
 - GitLab: self-hosted at `gitlab.example.com` with SSH alias `gitlab-ssh.example.com:2222`

**Logs**

`strace` output showing the rewritten remote URL:
```
execve("/usr/local/libexec/git-core/git-remote-https", [...], "origin", "https://gitlab-ssh.example.com/owner/repo.git")
```

Manual verification that sparse fetch works with the correct URL:
```shell
$ git -c init.defaultBranch=main init -q
$ git remote add origin ssh://git@gitlab-ssh.example.com:2222/owner/repo.git
$ git sparse-checkout init --no-cone
$ git sparse-checkout set agents/some-agent.agent.md
$ git fetch --filter=blob:none --depth=1 origin main  # succeeds
$ git checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
$ ls agents/some-agent.agent.md  # exists
```

**Additional context**

Workaround: switch the dependency to the HTTPS web URL and add a GitLab token:
```yaml
- git: https://gitlab.example.com/owner/repo.git
  path: agents/some-agent.agent.md
  type: gitlab
```
This requires HTTPS credentials for the GitLab instance rather than SSH keys.

issues.title: [BUG] Claude hook bundles drop nested package.json module metadata
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a Claude hook package places a JavaScript hook and its module metadata in a nested directory, APM deploys the JavaScript file but drops the nested `package.json`. APM then generates a CommonJS sidecar at the higher hook root, so Node executes the nested `.js` file with the wrong module semantics.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a Claude hook package with this layout:

   ```text
   hooks/
     hooks.json
     esm/
       entry.js
       package.json
   ```

2. Set `hooks/hooks.json` to:

   ```json
   {
     "hooks": {
       "SessionStart": [
         {
           "hooks": [
             {
               "type": "command",
               "command": "node ./esm/entry.js"
             }
           ]
         }
       ]
     }
   }
   ```

3. Set `hooks/esm/entry.js` to an ES module, for example:

   ```js
   import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
   writeFileSync(process.argv[2], "ok\\n");
   ```

4. Set `hooks/esm/package.json` to:

   ```json
   { "type": "module" }
   ```

5. Install the package into a project with Claude hooks enabled by running `apm install`.
6. Inspect the deployed hook under `.claude/hooks/<package>/hooks/esm/`.
7. Observe that `entry.js` is present, but `esm/package.json` is missing. The generated `.claude/hooks/<package>/hooks/package.json` contains `{"type": "commonjs"}`.
8. Run the deployed hook with Node and observe an import syntax error because the file is treated as CommonJS.

**Expected behavior**

APM should preserve the nested `hooks/esm/package.json`, or generate equivalent module metadata at the deployed `esm` boundary. Running the deployed `entry.js` should use ES module semantics and complete successfully.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows
 - Python Version: 3.12.13
 - APM Version: 0.30.0

**Logs**

APM reports no installation error. Executing the deployed JavaScript file produces a Node module syntax error such as:

```text
SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module
```

**Additional context**

`src/apm_cli/integration/hook_bundle.py` excludes every file named `package.json` in `iter_deployable_hook_bundle_files`, regardless of target. Claude passes `exclude_json_files=False`, but that option only controls the broader `.json` suffix filter and does not restore the skipped filename.

`_hook_module_type` searches the hook source root and its ancestors, not nested metadata directories. With no package-root or `hooks/package.json`, it therefore defaults to CommonJS and writes one sidecar at the deployed hook root.

This is distinct from #2824, which concerns missing `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and other files outside the selected hook script bundle. This defect concerns module metadata inside an otherwise selected bundle.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Show deployment targets and MCP counts in deps list
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When packages are installed for multiple agents, `apm deps list --all` does not show which targets each package was deployed to. Its primitive columns include Skills and Hooks, but no MCP server count, so MCP-only packages are difficult to understand from the table.

This was observed with APM 0.30.0. Users currently need to inspect manifests, lockfiles, or agent configuration files to answer these questions. `apm mcp list` lists registry servers rather than installed connections.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add two columns to `apm deps list`:

- **Targets:** each package's recorded deployment targets, such as `kiro, codex`. Use per-package deployment records rather than assigning every configured project target to every package. If records are unavailable, show an explicit unknown value.
- **MCPs:** the number of MCP servers bundled with the package, alongside the existing primitive counts. Include MCP-only packages even when they contain no skills.

As a related enhancement, support `--target kiro` to filter packages by their recorded target. Both columns and filtering should work for project installs, `--global`, and `--all`, preserving the scope distinction.

For example, a package deployed to Kiro and Codex with two MCP servers and no skills should show both targets, MCPs = 2, and Skills = 0. It should appear with `--target kiro` and be excluded when filtering for an agent it was not deployed to.

The target column describes recorded deployments, and the MCP count describes package contents; neither should imply that an MCP connection is currently healthy or authenticated. The two columns would be the priority, with filtering as a useful follow-up if needed.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Inspecting `apm.yml`, `apm.lock.yaml`, and each agent's MCP configuration works but makes a basic installed-package inventory cumbersome. Target filtering alone helps narrow results but does not make deployment targets discoverable in the default list.

**Additional context**

Related: #2070 concerns machine-readable CLI output, and #2948 concerns interactive removal of installed plugins. This request focuses on visibility in the dependency list.

issues.title: docs(reference): experimental flags table omits the openclaw flag
issues.body:
`docs/src/content/docs/reference/experimental.md` says at line 21 that the command will "List every registered flag with its current state", and the "Available flags" table at line 168 is that list. The table has 8 rows. `FLAGS` in `src/apm_cli/core/experimental.py:57` registers 9.

issues.title: [BUG] Marketplace uninstall aliases are lost after apm update
issues.body:
## Bug

After installing a plugin using `plugin@marketplace`, running `apm update` can lose the metadata needed to uninstall it by that original alias. This affects both project and global scope.

Installation stores canonical Git coordinates in `apm.yml` and records the marketplace alias in the lockfile. When update rebuilds the dependency's lock entry without rediscovering the marketplace, it drops `discovered_via` and `marketplace_plugin_name`. The dependency updates successfully, but uninstall can no longer resolve the alias offline and may abort at the existing registry/lock ownership guard.

## Reproduction

1. Register a marketplace and install a plugin using `plugin@marketplace`.
2. Advance the plugin's tracked Git branch.
3. Run `apm update --yes` in the same scope.
4. Inspect the lockfile: the revision advances, but the marketplace alias metadata is missing.
5. Unregister the marketplace and try to uninstall using the original alias.

The [automated project/global reproduction](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/95272ee97672743d95156736c277d5dc4c82309b/tests/integration/test_marketplace_update_provenance_lifecycle.py) uses a local Git remote and does not manually edit the consumer manifest or lockfile.

## Expected behavior

Updating the same dependency preserves its marketplace alias metadata while refreshing its revision and content hashes. Uninstalling by the original alias should continue to work without the marketplace being available.

## Environment

Originally reproduced with APM 0.30.0 and main at `e38261c5`, on macOS with Python 3.12.13 and the source-installed CLI.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Add to OpenCode a custom agent with tools as list
issues.body:
I tried to add a custom agent (arch-linux-expert.agent.md - https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/main/agents/arch-linux-expert.agent.md) for test; my targets are: copilot, antigravity, opencode.
For Antigravity there's another open issue about sub-agents (https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/2990), so this is for opencode.

[!] [awesome-copilot-arch-linux-expert] OpenCode agent 'awesome-copilot-arch-linux-expert/arch-linux-expert.agent.md' has tools as list; OpenCode requires a mapping of tool-name to boolean. OpenCode will reject this agent at load time. Fix: rewrite the frontmatter as 'tools: {Read: true, Grep: true}'.

I noticed lots of custom agents specify tools in list format, so this could be a problem with much of them.

issues.title: [BUG] install --dry-run falsely previews removal of a required transitive dependency
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

After a package with a transitive dependency is installed, rerunning `apm install --dry-run` from the unchanged consumer manifest omits the transitive package from its dependency preview and incorrectly says the transitive package's deployed files would be removed.

Running the same command without `--dry-run` resolves both packages and preserves the transitive files.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create three sibling directories named `consumer`, `parent`, and `child`.

2. Create `consumer/apm.yml`:

   ```yaml
   name: consumer
   version: 1.0.0
   targets:
     - copilot
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - ../parent
   ```

3. Create `parent/apm.yml`:

   ```yaml
   name: parent
   version: 1.0.0
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - ../child
   ```

4. Create `child/apm.yml`:

   ```yaml
   name: child
   version: 1.0.0
   ```

5. Add this instruction at both `parent/.apm/instructions/parent.instructions.md` and `child/.apm/instructions/child.instructions.md`:

   ```markdown
   ---
   applyTo: "**"
   ---
   # Instruction
   ```

6. From `consumer`, run `apm install --target copilot`. Both packages are installed:

   ```text
   [+] ../parent (local)
   [+] ../child (local)
   [*] Installed 2 APM dependencies
   ```

7. Without changing any manifest, run `apm install --target copilot --dry-run`:

   ```text
   [i] APM dependencies (1):
   [i]   - ../parent -> install
   [i] Files that would be removed (packages no longer in apm.yml): 1
   [i]   - .github/instructions/child.instructions.md
   ```

8. Run `apm install --target copilot` without `--dry-run`. It resolves both packages and leaves the child instruction unchanged.

**Expected behavior**

Dry-run reflects the real install plan: it includes the still-required transitive package and does not preview removal of its deployed files.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: macOS
- Python Version: 3.14.7
- APM Version: 0.31.0 installed with Homebrew; also reproduced with current `main`
- VSCode Version (if relevant): Not applicable

**Logs**

The relevant output is included in the reproduction above.

**Additional context**

The dry-run plan [collects only the root package's direct and development dependencies](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/98616b9430140275a3a7c8fefb25d8d111cecc4e/src/apm_cli/install/dry_run_plan.py#L27-L41) and [uses those dependencies as its orphan-preview intent](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/98616b9430140275a3a7c8fefb25d8d111cecc4e/src/apm_cli/install/dry_run_plan.py#L124-L133). The renderer passes that set to [`detect_orphans`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/98616b9430140275a3a7c8fefb25d8d111cecc4e/src/apm_cli/install/presentation/dry_run.py#L80-L100) and labels the result as files that would be removed because packages are no longer in `apm.yml`.

issues.title: [BUG] Annotated/signed tag resolves to tag object sha instead of peeled commit sha in marketplace source.sha
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`RefResolver.list_remote_refs` runs `git ls-remote --tags --heads` and `_parse_ls_remote_output` (`src/apm_cli/marketplace/ref_resolver.py`) explicitly drops every peeled (`^{}`) line:

```python
# Skip peeled tag objects (^{})
if refname.endswith("^{}"):
   continue
```

For a **lightweight** tag this is fine (the tag name IS the commit). For an **annotated/signed** tag, `git ls-remote` returns two lines for the same tag name:

```
e6c5e68b0064758b8106b83df41cf3829dde3216	refs/tags/v2.7.0
8b0c1d3699b8d83e87fe4605b378da20c41555e0	refs/tags/v2.7.0^{}
```

The first sha is the **tag object**; the discarded second line is the **peeled commit** it actually points to. Because the peeled line is always skipped, `RemoteRef.sha` for `v2.7.0` ends up being the tag object sha, not the commit sha.

This sha is then written into `marketplace.json`'s `source.sha` (via `apm pack`), and the plugin installer verifies the checked-out commit against it. Since checking out an annotated tag always lands on the peeled commit, this stored sha can **never** match, so installs/updates fail.

Skipping the `^{}` line is reasonable for tag-name matching/version resolution, but the sha recorded for that tag should be the peeled commit sha, not the raw tag object sha, whenever a `^{}` line is present for the same tag name.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create/find a repo with an annotated (optionally GPG/SSH-signed) tag, e.g. `git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "release"`.
2. Add it as a marketplace package with `version`/`tag_pattern` (no explicit `ref`).
3. Run `apm pack` and inspect the generated `source.sha` in `marketplace.json`.
4. Compare to `git ls-remote --tags <repo> "v1.0.0^{}"` (the real commit sha) - they differ.
5. See error installing/updating the package: a checkout-mismatch failure.

**Real-world case that surfaced this**

Hit this with the `caveman` plugin (`https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman`, annotated SSH-signed tag `v2.7.0`) in our internal marketplace: `apm pack` recorded the tag object sha instead of the peeled commit sha, breaking `/plugin update caveman` for all users with:

```
Failed: Error: Request plugins.update failed with message: Failed to fetch git plugin from the provided URL. Please verify that the
URL and reference are correct. Details: Pinned commit 'e6c5e68b0064758b8106b83df41cf3829dde3216' was not checked out: the pinned
object resolved to '8b0c1d3699b8d83e87fe4605b378da20c41555e0'
```

**Expected behavior**
`source.sha` should always be the peeled commit sha (the one a checkout of the tag actually produces), regardless of whether the tag is lightweight or annotated.

**Proposed fix**

In `_parse_ls_remote_output`, instead of discarding the `^{}` line, use it to correct the sha already recorded for the base tag name:

```python
def _parse_ls_remote_output(output: str) -> list[RemoteRef]:
   """Parse ``git ls-remote`` stdout into a list of ``RemoteRef``."""
   refs: list[RemoteRef] = []
   index_by_name: dict[str, int] = {}
   for line in output.splitlines():
     line = line.strip()
     if not line:
       continue
     parts = line.split("	", 1)
     if len(parts) != 2:
       continue
     sha, refname = parts[0].strip(), parts[1].strip()
     if not _SHA_RE.match(sha):
       continue
     if refname.endswith("^{}"):
       # Annotated/signed tag: this is the peeled commit the tag
       # actually resolves to on checkout. Replace the tag object
       # sha recorded for the base tag name instead of discarding
       # it, so source.sha matches what `git clone --branch <tag>`
       # checks out.
       base_name = refname[: -len("^{}")]
       idx = index_by_name.get(base_name)
       if idx is not None:
         refs[idx] = RemoteRef(name=base_name, sha=sha)
       continue
     index_by_name[refname] = len(refs)
     refs.append(RemoteRef(name=refname, sha=sha))
   return refs
```

This keeps the same ref names and list shape (no downstream caller needs to change: tag-pattern matching, semver resolution, `_resolve_explicit_ref` all still see `refs/tags/v2.7.0`), only the sha is corrected. Lightweight tags and branches are unaffected since git never emits a `^{}` line for them. A unit test should feed a tag+`^{}` pair into `_parse_ls_remote_output` and assert exactly one `RemoteRef` comes back for the tag name, with the peeled commit sha rather than the tag object sha.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows (reproduces on any OS; this is a git ref-resolution issue, not platform-specific)
 - Python Version: N/A (observed via the compiled `apm.exe`/`apm-cli` CLI, not a local Python invocation)
 - APM Version: 0.31.0
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A

**Logs**

See the error block above (checkout-mismatch).

**Additional context**
This is distinct from #2928 / PR #3044 (wrong remote queried for tags) and from #1822 (`{name}` tag-pattern matching) - neither touches sha correctness for annotated tags specifically.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-09-22
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-09-22
**APM Version**: 0.31.0 (e3e989c)
**Commands Inspected**: 32 top-level commands + 22 subcommand `--help` invocations (10 core commands, 6 `deps` subcommands, 4 `mcp` subcommands, 4 `config` subcommands, 2 `runtime` subcommands), plus error-path checks on invalid/missing arguments.

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 2 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm update` is documented as a "strict superset" of `apm deps update` but is missing `--legacy-skill-paths`
- **Command**: `apm update` vs `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md` (line 110) and `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/update.md` (line 22) both explicitly claim `apm update` is a "strict superset" of the deprecated `apm deps update`, listing the flags it covers (`-g/--global`, `[PACKAGES...]`, `--force`, `--parallel-downloads`, plus `--dry-run`/`--yes`). However `apm deps update --help` also documents `--legacy-skill-paths` ("Deploy skill files to per-client paths ... instead of the shared `.agents/skills/` directory"), and this flag does not exist on `apm update`.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm update --legacy-skill-paths
  Usage: apm update [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...
  Try 'apm update --help' for help.

  Error: No such option: --legacy-skill-paths
  ```
  `apm deps update --help` includes:
  ```
  --legacy-skill-paths          Deploy skill files to per-client paths (e.g.
                                 .cursor/skills/) instead of the shared
                                 .agents/skills/ directory. Compatibility flag
                                 for projects that need per-client skill
                                 layouts.
  ```
  Docs (deps.md line 110): "`apm deps update` is deprecated in favor of `apm update`, which is now a strict superset: it supports `-g/--global`, `[PACKAGES...]`, `--force`, and `--parallel-downloads`, plus an interactive plan, `--dry-run`, and `--yes`."
- **Suggested Fix**: Either add `--legacy-skill-paths` to `apm update`, or amend the "strict superset" claim in both `deps.md` and `update.md` to note the one flag that is not yet carried over (and clarify migration guidance for users who currently rely on `apm deps update --legacy-skill-paths`).

---

### Medium Severity

#### Inconsistent trailing punctuation in `apm mcp --help` command summaries
- **Command**: `apm mcp --help`
- **Problem**: In the `Commands:` list, `install` ends its one-line summary with a period while the other three subcommand summaries (`list`, `search`, `show`) do not, breaking the otherwise consistent style used across every other command group (`deps`, `config`, `runtime` all omit trailing periods in their one-line command summaries).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Commands:
    install  Add an MCP server to apm.yml.
    list     List all available MCP servers
    search   Search MCP servers in registry
    show     Show detailed MCP server information
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Drop the trailing period from the `install` subcommand's short help string so it matches the style of `list`/`search`/`show` (and the rest of the CLI's command-group summaries).

#### `--target` flag help text diverges in wording/detail between `apm update` and `apm deps update`
- **Command**: `apm update --help` vs `apm deps update --help`
- **Problem**: Both commands expose an equivalent `-t, --target TARGET` flag, but the help text differs materially in content, not just phrasing. `apm deps update --help` explains what `'agent-skills'`, `'antigravity'` do and what `'all'` excludes, and even reminds the user that "Deprecated: run 'apm update --target' instead." `apm update --help`'s version omits the `agent-skills`/`antigravity`/`all`-exclusion explanation entirely and instead documents the resolution-order chain, which `deps update` doesn't mention. A user pointed from the deprecated command to the replacement loses information about target semantics that only exists in the deprecated command's help.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm deps update --help
  -t, --target TARGET           Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                                 ... 'agent-skills' deploys to .agents/skills/
                                 (cross-client). 'antigravity' (alias 'agy')
                                 deploys to .agents/ and is explicit-only --
                                 not part of 'all'. 'all' excludes
                                 agent-skills, antigravity, hermes,
                                 experimental targets, and intellij; ...
                                 Deprecated: run 'apm update --target' instead.

  # apm update --help
  -t, --target TARGET           Agent target(s) to update for. Values: ...
                                 Comma-separated for multiple: --target
                                 claude,cursor. Highest-priority entry in the
                                 resolution chain (--target > apm.yml
                                 targets: > apm config set target ... >
                                 auto-detect).
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Since `apm deps update` explicitly tells users to switch to `apm update --target`, `apm update`'s `--target` help should retain the `agent-skills`/`antigravity`/`all`-exclusion explanation (or at least link to `apm compile --help`'s fuller wording) so no information is lost in the migration.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm compile --target` help includes extra target-behavior detail that sibling commands' `--target` flags omit
- **Command**: `apm compile --help`, `apm install --help`, `apm deps update --help`, `apm update --help`
- **Problem**: All four commands share the same `-t/--target` flag and largely the same list of target values, but each has a differently-detailed explanation appended (some mention `agent-skills` deploy path and IntelliJ notes, some mention resolution-order chains, some mention deprecation pointers). This is not wrong, but it's a genuine style inconsistency: a flag shared across 4+ commands should ideally have one canonical explanation with only the command-specific parts varying.
- **Evidence**: See target-flag text differences quoted above and in `compile.txt`/`install.txt`/`deps_update.txt`/`update.txt` capture.
- **Suggested Fix**: Consider factoring a single canonical `--target` values/semantics blurb shared by all commands that expose it, with only command-specific caveats (e.g., IntelliJ-is-MCP-only for `install`, deprecation notice for `deps update`) appended per command.

#### `-v, --verbose` short descriptions vary slightly in specificity across commands
- **Command**: All commands exposing `-v, --verbose`
- **Problem**: The wording for `--verbose` differs across commands without an obvious content reason: `"Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis"` (compile), `"Show detailed update information"` (deps update), `"Show detailed output"` (mcp search/show, run), `"Show detailed installation information"` (install), `"Show detailed removal information"` (uninstall), `"Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics"` (update). Most are fine as command-specific descriptions, but `mcp search`, `mcp show`, and `run` all use the generic, uninformative `"Show detailed output"` with no hint of what extra detail verbose mode actually reveals, unlike every other command.
- **Evidence**: See the aggregated `--verbose` grep output across all captured `--help` files.
- **Suggested Fix**: Replace the generic `"Show detailed output"` on `mcp search`, `mcp show`, and `run` with a one-line description of what verbose mode actually surfaces for each (mirroring the specificity used by `install`, `uninstall`, and `update`).

---

### Clean Areas

- **Installation & version check**: `apm --version` and `apm --help` work correctly; version 0.31.0 (e3e989c) reported cleanly.
- **Top-level command inventory**: All 32 top-level commands returned by `apm --help` match 1:1 with the commands documented in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/index.md`'s phase table (project setup, inspect/audit, compile/integrate, cache/config, run, author/distribute, governance, experimental). No orphaned or undocumented top-level commands found.
- **`apm config`**: `get`, `list`, `set`, `unset` subcommands all behave and are documented exactly as the CLI reports; `apm config get` (no key) and `apm config list` are confirmed functionally identical, matching the docs' explicit claim.
- **`apm mcp`, `apm deps`, `apm runtime` subcommand surfaces**: Every subcommand's flags, defaults, and one-line descriptions cross-checked cleanly against `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/mcp.md`, `deps.md`, and `runtime.md` (aside from the two medium findings above).
- **Error handling / exit behavior**: `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (missing arg), `apm config set` (missing args), `apm mcp show` (missing arg), `apm runtime setup badruntime`, and `apm uninstall nonexistent-pkg` all produce clean, well-formatted usage/error messages with correct non-zero exit codes (2 for click usage errors) -- no stack traces observed anywhere.
- **README.md cross-reference**: All CLI commands and install flows mentioned in `README.md` (`apm install`, `apm compile -t copilot`, `apm install --mcp`, `apm marketplace add`, etc.) exist and behave as described.
- **No typos, TODOs, or placeholder text** found in any captured help string.

issues.title: [BUG] Transitive git+path monorepo dependency fails "not a valid APM package" on 0.29.1+ (regression from 0.29.0)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`apm install` fails to resolve a transitive `git:` + `path:` dependency when both the top-level package and its dependency are subdirectories ("virtual packages") of the same monorepo, each with their own valid `apm.yml`. The resolver reports the dependency as invalid against the **bare repository root** (no path), even though:

- The declared dependency correctly specifies `path: packages/pkg-shared`, which **does** contain a valid `apm.yml`.
- The dependency package's own `apm.yml` declares `dependencies: apm: []` — it has no further dependencies of its own that could explain a second resolution attempt.

This worked correctly on `0.29.0` and regressed starting with `0.29.1`. It is still broken on the current latest (`0.31.0`).

### To Reproduce

Repo layout (relevant parts) in a monorepo `your-org/your-monorepo`:
```
packages/
  pkg-a/
    apm.yml
  pkg-shared/
    apm.yml   # dependencies: apm: []
```

`packages/pkg-a/apm.yml`:
```yaml
name: 'pkg-a'
version: '1.0.0'
targets:
  - 'copilot'
dependencies:
  apm:
    - git: https://github.com/your-org/your-monorepo
      path: packages/pkg-shared
      ref: main
```

Run:
```bash
apm install your-org/your-monorepo/packages/pkg-a --target copilot --verbose
```

### Actual result

```
[>] Resolving your-monorepo-pkg-a...
[>] Resolving your-monorepo-pkg-shared...
  Failed to resolve transitive dep your-org/your-monorepo (via your-monorepo-pkg-a > your-monorepo-pkg-shared): Invalid APM package your-org/your-monorepo:
  - Not a valid APM package: no apm.yml, SKILL.md, hooks, or plugin structure found in <hash>. Ensure the package has SKILL.md (skill bundle), apm.yml + .apm/ (APM package), or plugin.json (Claude plugin) at its root.
[x] Installation failed with 1 error(s). No install transaction changes were committed.
```

The error names the **bare repo** (`your-org/your-monorepo`, no path segment), not `packages/pkg-shared`. The sparse checkout itself materializes correctly (`perf: subdir .../packages/pkg-shared sparse=packages/pkg-shared`), so the failure is specifically in the validation/graph step, not the clone.

### Expected behavior

The dependency should resolve using the declared `path: packages/pkg-shared` and install successfully, exactly as it did on `0.29.0`.

### Environment

Tested with a clean `apm cache clean` before each run:

| APM version | Result |
|---|---|
| 0.29.0 | ✅ Works |
| 0.29.1 | ❌ Fails (same signature) |
| 0.30.0 | ❌ Fails (same signature) |
| 0.31.0 (latest) | ❌ Fails (same signature) |

- OS: macOS
- Install method: `pip install apm-cli==<version>`, isolated venv per version

### Additional context

- I also tried rewriting the dependency using the documented monorepo-sibling sentinel `git: parent` (per the [manifest schema](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/manifest-schema/#412-object-form)) instead of the explicit URL. This does **not** fix the issue on 0.31.0, and it additionally **breaks the previously-working 0.29.0 install** with the identical error — `git: parent` appears to expand to the same `repo_url`/`virtual_path` coordinates as the explicit form, hitting the same bug.
- Related but distinct reports I found while investigating:
  - #2912 — "path: dep validates apm.yml at sparse subdir, not repo root" — closed as not-planned/intentional, but describes a *different* scenario (path pointing at a non-package subdirectory with no manifest of its own). In our case both subdirectories are valid standalone packages.
  - #2888 — "skills: subset install fails on 0.29+/0.30" — fixed in 0.31.0 via #2891, but that mechanism is `skills:` subset selection, not `git:`+`path:` virtual packages.
  - #2877 — registry-based transitive dependency resolution bug — unrelated mechanism (registry, not git).

Given the clean version bisection (0.29.0 passes, 0.29.1 fails), a diff between those two tags in the transitive-dependency validation/graph code should narrow this down quickly.
